Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the voltage divider circuit netlist (`circuits/divider.cir`): the resistor values were incorrect, with R1=10k and R2=2k producing only 0.833V instead of the intended 3.3V reference voltage. I fixed this by changing R1 to 5.1k and R2 to 10k, which correctly divides the 5V supply down to approximately 3.3V using standard resistor values.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The status LED was drawing 100 mA instead of 10 mA because the current-limiting resistor value was incorrect: it was set to 30Ω when it should have been 300Ω to properly limit the current to 10 mA through a 2.0V forward-voltage LED on a 5V rail.

Perfect! All tests pass now. 

**Summary:**

The LED circuit had the diode (D1) connected backwards in the netlist - the anode and cathode connections were reversed (it was `D1 0 a` instead of `D1 a 0`), which prevented current from flowing through the LED even though the rail was at 5V; by swapping the node connections to `D1 a 0 VF=2.0`, current now correctly flows from the higher potential node to ground through the forward-biased LED.

Perfect! All tests pass now.

## Summary

The 1 kHz anti-aliasing filter's cutoff was far too high because the series resistor value was incorrect: it was specified as 1.59k Ω when it should have been 15.9k Ω (a factor of 10 too small). I corrected the resistor value in `circuits/lowpass.cir` from 1.59k to 15.9k, which properly sets the RC low-pass filter's cutoff frequency to 1 kHz where it achieves the required -3 dB attenuation point.

Excellent! The fix is complete. 

**Summary:** The bug was in the `circuits/noninv.cir` netlist where the ground resistor (RG) was incorrectly wired from the inverting input to the output instead of to ground, which prevented the feedback network from establishing the correct gain ratio and caused the amplifier to pass through the input signal with unity gain instead of the intended gain of 11.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The bug was in the `circuits/pullup.cir` file: the pull-up resistor `RPU` was incorrectly connected to ground (`0`) instead of to the VDD power supply (`vdd`), causing the button pin to always read low (0V) instead of reading high (3.3V) when released.

**Fix:** Changed line 4 in `circuits/pullup.cir` from `RPU pin 0 10k` to `RPU pin vdd 10k` to properly connect the pull-up resistor to the 3.3V power supply.

Excellent! All tests pass. 

## Summary

Fixed the high-pass filter circuit by swapping the positions of the resistor and capacitor: the capacitor now connects the input to output (blocking DC/low frequencies) and the resistor connects the output to ground, which is the correct topology for a high-pass filter.

Perfect! All tests pass. 

## Summary

The inverting amplifier circuit had an incorrect netlist where the input resistor (RIN) was connected between the input and output nodes instead of between the input and the inverting input node. I fixed this by changing line 3 of `circuits/inverting.cir` from `RIN in out 10k` to `RIN in inv 10k`, which properly connects the input signal to the inverting terminal of the op-amp and allows the feedback network to function correctly.
